learning_outcomes.text: Students can analyze thermodynamic processes using material data, diagrams, and tables, represent them computationally, systematically balance energy exchange between thermodynamic systems, and interpret the results.
Students can define and apply fundamental thermodynamic concepts such as systems, equilibrium, state variables, changes of state, processes, and process variables work and heat.
Students understand the thermal and caloric equations of state for ideal gases.
Students are able to establish and solve material and mass balances for simple systems and mixing processes.
Students can apply and interpret the 1st law of thermodynamics to closed, stationary, and moving systems, as well as to steady flow processes.
Students can calculate simple changes of state for ideal gases and represent them in various diagrams (e.g., p-v, T-s, and h-s diagrams).
Students know the significance of the 2nd law of thermodynamics and can apply the concepts of entropy and irreversibility to processes.
Students can analyze and evaluate simple reversible cyclic processes, especially regarding work, power, and efficiency.
Students understand the thermodynamic properties of real fluids, can represent states and changes of state in the two-phase region, and utilize material data from tables and diagrams.
Students know the fundamentals of heat transfer and can describe and calculate heat transfer mechanisms such as conduction, convection, and radiation.

syllabus_topics: Basic concepts of thermodynamics such as system, equilibrium, thermal and caloric state variables, changes of state, processes, process variables work and heat
Ideal gases: Thermal / Caloric equation of state for ideal gases
Material and mass balances of simple mixtures
1st law of thermodynamics: stationary / moving closed systems, steady flow processes, specific heat capacity, simple changes of state for ideal gases and their representation in various diagrams
Cyclic processes: simple reversible comparison processes; concepts: work, power, efficiency
Real fluids, changes of state in the two-phase region, representation in various diagrams, material data calculations and tables
assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded upon successful completion of the module examination.
